request.user:
Subject: Physics
Question type: integer answer (no options)

A wooden cube just floats inside water when a 800 g mass is placed on it. When the mass is removed, the cube is 2 cm above the water level. What is the size of the side of the cube (in cm) ?

result.working:
With the 800 g mass on it, the cube is just fully submerged. Removing the mass makes the cube rise until 2 cm sticks out above the water.
The buoyant force lost equals the weight of the mass removed: a² × 2 × ρ_w × g = 0.8 × g.
In cgs units with ρ_w = 1 g/cm³: a² × 2 = 800, so a² = 400.
Therefore a = 20 cm.
result.note: 'Just floats' is taken to mean the cube is fully submerged, with its top level with the water surface, when the mass is on it.
